decision_conditions: The applicant has failed to present plans which clearly depict the proposed development. Inconsistencies between the submitted ground (drawing ref: 25-878-P03, revision A) and first floor plans (drawing ref: 25-878-P04, revision A) create uncertainty regarding the intended form and extent of the proposal. This lack of clarity adds to concerns about the appropriateness of the design and risks prejudicing third parties who may otherwise have wished to comment on the application. As a result, the proposed development cannot be accurately assessed, and it cannot be demonstrated that it would comply with the Development Plan. As such, the proposal is contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024)Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021);Policies SP2 and DMD1 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development, by reason of its excessive bulk, mass, scale, design and siting, would result in a disproportionate and overly large extension that fails to respect the proportions and character of the host dwelling. The combined porch, two storey side extension and part single, part two storey rear extensions would cumulatively overwhelm the original property, effectively doubling its internal floorspace and creating a footprint larger than the existing dwelling, amounting to overdevelopment of the site. The depth, width and wraparound form of the rear extensions, together with the reduced spacing caused by the side extension, would disrupt the established pattern of modest rear projections, consistent building lines and clear visual breaks that characterise the terrace row, resulting in an incongruous form of development. The proposal also introduces a fragmented and visually discordant roofscape, including multiple differing roof forms and an irregular catslide type arrangement to the front, which fails to reflect the coherent pitched and hipped roof profiles typical of the surrounding area. This would create a disjointed appearance when viewed from both the front and side elevations. As a result, the development would appear incongruous and out of keeping with the established character of the locality. The proposal is therefore contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies D1 and D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2, DMD1, DMD5 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)The Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (February 2012)

The proposed development, by reason of the depth, height and siting of the single storey rear extension along the shared boundary with No. 4 East Park Close, would result in an unacceptable loss of daylight, increased overshadowing and an overbearing sense of enclosure to that neighbouring property. The first floor rear extension would further add to the massing resulting in a development that appears unduly dominant when viewed from No. 4. The proposal therefore fails to safeguard the amenity of neighbouring occupiers. This impact would be unacceptable and thus is contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024)Part D of policy D6 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies DMD1 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)
borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
description: Construction of front porch, a two storey side extension and a part single storey part two storey rear extension
